subtitle: In Pratishthana’s halls, a Satavahana king gathers the songs of many hearts.

panels.shot: majestic frontal wide of the king on a stone terrace above the Godavari valley at dusk
panels.action: King Hala of Pratishthana stands robed in Satavahana splendor on a high terrace, river and distant town below, palm-leaf manuscripts stacked beside him, as unseen voices seem to rise from the land.

dialogue.text: In the age of the Satavahanas, King Hala of Pratishthana is remembered not for conquests, but for gathering seven hundred Prakrit songs of love and life.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन काल में प्रतिष्ठान का राजा हाल विजयों नहीं, सात सौ प्राकृत प्रेम और जीवन गीतों के लिए याद है।

panels.shot: broad establishing aerial of the Deccan plateau and Godavari river basin
panels.action: The camera glides above the sunlit Deccan plateau: fields, forest and the wide curve of the Godavari river, with trading boats and small settlements dotting its banks.

dialogue.text: From the first centuries of the Common Era, Satavahana power stretches across the Deccan, binding river valleys, caravan routes and villages in a changing world of trade and faith.

i18n.hi: ईसा की शुरुआती सदियों में सातवाहन शक्ति दक्कन में फैलकर नदियों, काफ़िलों और गाँवों को बदलती व्यापार–आस्था की दुनिया में बाँधती है।

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Pratishthana city walls and gates bustling with activity
panels.action: Pratishthana’s fortified walls rise above the river, busy gates admitting traders with pack animals, monks in ochre robes, craftsmen, and farmers carrying baskets of grain.

dialogue.text: At Pratishthana on the Godavari, the Satavahana capital hums with merchants from the coast, monks from cave monasteries, and farmers whose seasons drive the kingdom’s pulse.

i18n.hi: गोदावरी किनारे प्रतिष्ठान में राजधानी तट से आए व्यापारी, गुफ़ा विहारों के भिक्षु और मौसम से चलने वाले किसानोँ से गूँजती है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of the king seated on a simple but dignified throne amid advisors
panels.action: King Hala sits on a carved stone throne, dressed in dignified but unostentatious royal garments; ministers, scribes and monks stand nearby, scrolls and copper-plate documents in their hands.

dialogue.text: Satavahana kings rule by balancing land grants, caravan taxes and religious patronage. Amid them is Hala, remembered in later tradition as a ruler who turned his ear to everyday speech.

i18n.hi: सातवाहन राजा ज़मीन दान, काफ़िला कर और धर्म–संरक्षण सँभालकर राज करते हैं; उन्हीं में हाल है, जिसे आम बोली सुनने वाला राजा कहा गया।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the king’s thoughtful profile as Sanskrit and Prakrit texts lie before him
panels.action: Close on King Hala’s profile in lamplight, eyes intent; before him lie two sets of manuscripts—elegant Sanskrit palm leaves and simpler Maharashtri Prakrit bundles—while a scribe kneels nearby.

dialogue.text: In his age, Sanskrit grows as the language of gods and royal display. Yet Prakrit—the speech of markets and fields—carries the everyday music of desire, quarrel and teasing.

i18n.hi: उसके समय संस्कृत देवताओं और दरबार की भाषा बनती है, पर बाज़ार और खेतों की प्राकृत में रोज़ की चाह, झगड़ा और चुहल गूँजती है।

panels.shot: intimate interior wide of a small court gathering with village women and bards before the king
panels.action: Within an airy hall, King Hala sits at the head while village women, a wandering bard, and a young court poet stand before him, their clothes rustic and varied, faces curious but unafraid.

dialogue.text: Later memory places Hala at the center of an unusual court. Here, not only polished Brahmins but farmers’ daughters and wandering singers can release brief, sharp verses in Prakrit.

i18n.hi: बाद की याद में हाल का दरबार कुछ अलग दिखता है; यहाँ सिर्फ़ घिसे–पिटे ब्राह्मण नहीं, किसान बेटियाँ और घूमते गायक भी तेज़, छोटे प्राकृत पद छोड़ सकते हैं।

panels.shot: medium on the king leaning forward to listen to a woman poet reciting
panels.action: King Hala leans forward, eyes bright, as a young woman in modest village dress raises her hand in a subtle gesture, lips parted mid-recitation, her companions watching nervously.

dialogue.speaker: king_hala_and_the_sattasai_poets
dialogue.text: Speak as you do in the fields and courtyards. Do not polish your tongue for me.

i18n.hi: जैसे खेतों और आँगनों में बोलते हो वैसे ही बोलो, मेरे लिए ज़बान मत सजाओ।

panels.shot: tight shot of a palm-leaf being inscribed by a court scribe with the king observing
panels.action: A scribe sits cross-legged, carefully incising Prakrit lines onto a palm leaf; King Hala stands behind, hands folded, watching each stroke as if weighing the words themselves.

dialogue.text: Tradition names Hala as the collector of seven hundred gāthās. Modern scholars see a slow anthology: many poets, many decades, later redactors shaping what his name came to represent.

i18n.hi: परंपरा हाल को सात सौ गाथाओं का संग्राहक कहती है; आज के विद्वान इसे धीमी संकलन मानते हैं—कई कवि, कई दशक, बाद के संपादकों ने उसके नाम में रूप दिया।

panels.shot: cross-cut montage wide showing countryside scenes that match different poems while the king studies
panels.action: Split composition: on one side King Hala studies palm leaves; on the other, vignettes of village life—a woman at a well glancing toward a path, lovers on a riverbank, a wife waiting at a doorway.

dialogue.text: The Gaha Sattasai holds brief flashes of life: a girl mocking her timid lover, a wife angry at a husband’s delay, a farmer’s daughter measuring desire against duty and gossip.

i18n.hi: गहा सतसई में जीवन की झलकियाँ चमकती हैं—डरपोक प्रेमी को चिढ़ाती लड़की, देर से लौटे पति पर भड़की पत्नी, चाह और फ़र्ज़ को आँकती किसान–बेटी।

panels.shot: medium shot of the king smiling slightly as a mischievous poem is recited
panels.action: King Hala sits with a small circle of poets as an older woman recites a playful verse; some courtiers look shocked, but the king’s mouth curves into an amused, approving smile.

dialogue.text: Many verses speak in women’s voices, teasing and direct about desire and frustration. In this imagined court, a king nods as the propriety of elite halls bends toward the candor of courtyards.

i18n.hi: कई पद स्त्रियों की आवाज़ में हैं, चाह और खीझ पर बेबाक चुहल से भरे; इस रचे दरबार में राजा सिर हिलाता है, ऊँचे सभागारों की लाज आँगनों की साफ़गोई के आगे झुकती है।

panels.shot: low-angle interior showing Brahmin scholars debating before the king
panels.action: A group of Brahmin scholars in fine garments stand before King Hala, some gesturing toward a Sanskrit manuscript, others toward the Prakrit anthology, their faces animated in thoughtful dispute.

dialogue.text: Around Hala’s name later gather debates on language. Can Prakrit, the ‘speech of snakes’ in some eyes, rise beside Sanskrit? The anthology quietly answers by enduring in royal memory.

i18n.hi: हाल के नाम के आस–पास भाषा पर बहसें जमती हैं—क्या कुछ के लिए ‘साँपों की ज़बान’ प्राकृत संस्कृत के साथ उठ सकती है? उत्तर खुद संग्रह देता है, राज–याद में टिककर।

panels.shot: close-up of the king’s hand placing the Prakrit manuscript among other royal treasures
panels.action: Close on King Hala’s hand as he places the bound Prakrit manuscript in a carved chest alongside royal seals, treaties and religious donations, treating it as part of his realm’s wealth.

dialogue.text: Whether or not he chose each verse, the Hala tradition signals this: a Satavahana court counts short Prakrit love songs among its treasured instruments of prestige and identity.

i18n.hi: चाहे उसने हर पद खुद चुना हो या नहीं, हाल की परंपरा यह तो कहती है: सातवाहन दरबार छोटी–छोटी प्राकृत प्रेम–गीतों को भी अपनी प्रतिष्ठा और पहचान का औज़ार मानता है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide of scribes copying the anthology over generations
panels.action: In a dim archive, generations of scribes in different dress sit at long benches, copying the Gaha Sattasai onto fresh palm leaves as older bundles darken and crack on high shelves.

dialogue.text: Across the second to fourth centuries and beyond, redactors and scribes reshape the anthology. New poems enter, some fall away, yet the frame of Hala’s seven hundred songs remains.

i18n.hi: दूसरी से चौथी सदी और आगे तक संपादक और लिपिक इस संग्रह को बदलते रहते हैं; नए पद जुड़ते, कुछ छूटते हैं, पर हाल के सात सौ गीतों का ढाँचा बना रहता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of a Gupta-era court poet reading from the Sattasai
panels.action: In a later, more ornate court, a Gupta-era poet stands before nobles, holding a palm-leaf bundle, reciting a Prakrit verse as listeners nod in appreciation, banners and sculptures in the background.

dialogue.text: By the early centuries of the Gupta age, Maharashtri Prakrit is firmly linked with romance. Poets across regions draw on Hala’s anthology as they shape their own courtly lyrics.

i18n.hi: गुप्त युग की शुरुआती सदियों में महाराष्ट्रि प्राकृत का रंग पक्का प्रेम से जुड़ जाता है; अलग–अलग क्षेत्रों के कवि अपने दरबारी गीतों में हाल की सतसई से सहारा लेते हैं।

panels.shot: wide of Bana in his study with manuscripts, including one labeled by a small emblem of Hala
panels.action: The writer Bana sits in a simple study, surrounded by manuscripts, a small emblem of Hala drawn on one bundle; he turns to it thoughtfully while composing, lamps casting long shadows.

dialogue.text: By the seventh century, Bana’s words show that Hala’s Sattasai is known in the north. The anthology travels, remembered as a Satavahana king’s legacy of brief, piercing gāthās.

i18n.hi: सातवीं सदी तक बाण की लिखत दिखाती है कि हाल की सतसई उत्तर में भी जानी जाती है; सातवाहन राजा की तेज़, चुभती गाथाओं की यह धरोहर दूर–दूर तक घूमती है।

panels.shot: scholarly close-up of a modern researcher examining a fragile palm-leaf in a library
panels.action: In a modern archive, a researcher in simple clothes gently examines a fragile palm-leaf manuscript, magnifying glass and soft brushes nearby, as other catalogued bundles line the shelves.

dialogue.text: Today, scholars read through layers of manuscript and memory, careful not to credit all seven hundred verses to one hand, yet tracing how a royal name anchors a many-voiced tradition.

i18n.hi: आज विद्वान पांडुलिपियों और यादों की परतें पढ़ते हैं; सतर्क हैं कि सारे सात सौ पद एक ही हाथ को न दें, पर देखते हैं कि एक राज–नाम कैसे बहु–स्वर परंपरा को बाँधता रहा।

panels.shot: contemplative medium shot of King Hala on the terrace at night, stars above, distant village lights below
panels.action: King Hala stands again on his terrace under a starry sky, the distant glow of village fires below, the Prakrit manuscript cradled in his arms as if listening to the murmurs rising from the land.

dialogue.text: Hala’s story reminds us: a court becomes truly great when it gathers and preserves the speech of many lives, letting even brief village songs echo alongside the proclamations of kings.

i18n.hi: हाल की कहानी याद दिलाती है—दरबार सचमुच महान तब बनता है जब वह कई जीवनों की बोली समेटकर बचाए, ताकि छोटे गाँव के गीत भी राज–फ़रमानों के साथ गूँज सकें।

title_i18n.en: The King Who Gathered Seven Hundred Songs
title_i18n.hi: सात सौ गीत समेटने वाला राजा

subtitle_i18n.en: In Pratishthana’s halls, a Satavahana king gathers the songs of many hearts.
subtitle_i18n.hi: प्रतिष्ठान की दीवारों में सातवाहन राजा कई दिलों के गीत जुटाता है।
